title: AI made my 2026 game better than my 2014 one in every way I can measure. The 2014 one did 13.5M installs, the 2026 one has none. I published 13 years of Play Console data. Is discovery the whole problem now?
author: Firm-Independent9992
selftext:
In September 2014 a game I made alone crossed a million installs on day 27. I drew the art myself and you could tell. No budget, no publisher.

  
This year I came back and released a new game. AI does the art and the music, I use AI coding tools, and the game is better than the 2014 one in every way I can measure. It has effectively zero installs.

  
I wanted to know what actually changed, so I exported thirteen years of my Play Console data and published all of it, raw files included:

  
[https://games.lukicengineering.com/blog/2013-vs-2026/?src=aigamedev](https://games.lukicengineering.com/blog/2013-vs-2026/?src=aigamedev)

  
AI is the reason the art and music exist at all, and I ship code faster with it. None of that helps anyone find the game. In 2014 the store itself put new apps in front of people. In 2026 it amplifies traffic you bring from outside and adds almost none of its own, so the bottleneck moved from making to reaching.

  
The CSVs are at the bottom of the page if you want to check the numbers. Happy to answer anything about the AI workflow or either era.

comments.author: Unnamed-3891
comments.body: Competing for people's limited time is harder than ever. I find myself coming back to Diablo and Call of Duty often. For others it's GTA. There was and article some time ago that explained that more than 60% of players time is actually spent playing 10 year old or even older games.

replies.author: KhaosPT
replies.body: Me playing ff tactics advance again. But discovery has never been worse, on the Google app store if you type the name of a game, it will first list all the ads and the exact game with the exact name might not even show until you scroll a lot. That's just how broken the system is

replies.author: IAgreeGames
replies.body: What hope does anyone have to being found? We should be building new app stores that focus on the customer again. AI is making things so available, let's build new and better store fronts with it (to monetize of course I people gotta eat, but also make better UXs)

replies.author: PlaidWorld
replies.body: No one would use or find your app store either...

replies.author: Firm-Independent9992
replies.body: The system has worked this way since 2017, as the graphs I posted show. At least that's been the case with my games. With the AI tools available today, it's much easier to research things, and I probably did five times more preparation than I used to. But it didn't help. Keywords, a better description, following the recommended practices for growth, none of it worked.

replies.author: TheSpanxxx
replies.body:
I used to love browsing the Xbox game store and would find interesting games and give indie games a shot all the time. Then monetization of the store itself and algorithm based searches killed everything. Now everything is a paid result, even when you aren't aware it is, and every single thing put in front of you is tracked and fed through an algorithm designed to make sure you will see what they think you are most likely to click on. 

And the sheer volume of absolute garbage in online game stores is just utterly astounding.  Shameful, even. It's exhausting and why I tend to only play new releases on massive titles/IP I'm already familiar with, games that are WOM referral, or standby favorites. I'll try a random title here and there after reading threads of reviews from enough people it feels like I'm not just trying to be convinced by an advertising bot-army.

replies.author: Firm-Independent9992
replies.body: Honestly, if it hadn’t become this easy to bring ideas to life and test them, I probably wouldn’t have even considered getting back into game development after the decline that started in 2017. It looks like the market has simply become saturated, but Google Play itself has also become so disconnected from indie developers that sometimes it feels like everything they do is designed to make people give up as quickly as possible.

replies.author: No_Care5798
replies.body: Not only that, but there’s a LOT of AI garbage being published. If the art is recognizable as AI it generally gets avoided simply because of that.

replies.author: porkchoppolous
replies.body: Yeah I second this, when I take time a to game a lot of the time Its Project Zomboid or Rimworld. Both very old games.

comments.author: Vonterribad
comments.body: AI pushes everything to the midpoint which is effectively ignored.

comments.author: Jolva
comments.body: I'm in my late forties and have extra income but very little extra time. If a game that's easy to pick up gets on my radar I buy it. I don't have time to learn something like Anno today, but I bought Ball X Pitt on two platforms when it came out. I'm sure there are others like me. You just gotta find us with marketing.

comments.author: _BreakingGood_
comments.body:
Based on the screenshots: 

In 2014, this would be a cool looking, unique game. 

In 2026, while it does look visually decent, it looks like something Claude could create in a few prompts. 

Unfortunately AI has raised the bar, and games that used to be fine are now very easily overlooked.

replies.author: gcube2000
replies.body: That and a lot of people don’t want games that look like they were created with AI.

comments.author: DifferentComposer878
comments.body: It’s just the nature of progress and discovery issues even before AI. I had a game on iOS in 2010 and I was featured in the news and on the radio in Miami.  Sold well for a 99 cent game. I think I made a few hundred buck. The game was bad. Four years later I made an infinitely better version of the game and gave it away for free with IAP. Couldn’t get press coverage and had 20 downloads.

comments.author: yn3kk
comments.body: Yes, discovery and marketing has been the sole problem of most of good products that did not reach the consumer. That is the case for any industry and commodity.

comments.author: mantrakid
comments.body: yes 2014 was a different time. those days are gone.

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body: It's not just the AI problem. You made a game in a saturated genre and the trailer nor screenshots differentiate it. If there is something special about the game, a person can't tell just by looking.

comments.author: smallandnormal
comments.body: If Tetris were released in this day and age, the number of downloads would be zero.

comments.author: EC36339
comments.body: Your 2014 game had 12 years to be discovered and downloaded. Your 2026 game had less than one.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body: Just stating facts. Don't complain to me.

replies.author: EC36339
replies.body:
A game from 2014 was released 13 years ago.

A game from 2026 was released less than 1 year ago.

Do you need a graph to understand that?

comments.author: Nasilbitatbirakti
comments.body: You had much less competition back in the day and the sheer amount of games you have to compete increased expenentially. In 2014 you maybe had 100 similar games, now you have 100000 similar games. Just my opinion but you shouldn't waste your time with game dev unless you have enough originality in your idea. A slightly different version of the trope that's been done a million times isn't something you want to waste your time on.

comments.author: dx0ne
comments.body: Youve wrote that art doesn't help find games. So no true. Today its even more important. Its just your game looks like a prototype. Look at indie scene - bar is super high, was fir quite few years, ai has nothing to do.

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: 1 and a half star review I think was your issue big dog

comments.author: xircom2
comments.body: AI game dev is exciting, but let's face it. Most games are half-baked mini-games that last half an hour. People need to start focusing on quality.

comments.author: AhriKyuubi
comments.body: The scene was pretty new in 2014, now there are a lot of games compared to a decade a go

comments.author: Melodic-Hippo5536
comments.body:
Too much competition. Years ago several countries decided that they would subsidize the video game industry as a way to create “high-tech” jobs in their countries. Even before agentic coding became available, the competition has been growing more fierce. For every successful game, a bunch of copycat games launch within a few weeks or months. Slop has been a thing in this industry years before AI and vibe coding became a thing.

Also, free-to-play has become a new norm. So you have to do something different to make people willing to pay before they play.

comments.author: gcube2000
comments.body: It’s not just discovery, although that’s a big part of it. It’s also people have far more distractions than they did in 2014. And there is an absolute onslaught of new products with AI. Honestly I don’t know what’s worth pivoting to in this current age, but indie game dev is an absolute shit-show dead end right now.

comments.author: Standard_Text480
comments.body: Everyone has a boner against AI slop, even if the game didn't exist at all would be their preference

comments.author: Lavio00
comments.body: Croski are you kidding me? Back then an app where you tilted your phone to drink a ”beer” was downloaded millions of times. A lot has changed since then, a glorified shooting range wont cut it when we’ve got balatro, vampire survivors and slay the spire on phones.

comments.author: Miniburner
comments.body: Nobody wants a game with ai art or music or animations or anything. It has nothing to do with reaching people. It got to people, and people said NO

replies.author: aigamedev-ModTeam
replies.body: Be respectful. Removed for AI Art or Artist bashing.

comments.author: kasikciozan
comments.body: to be completely honest, your game looks super boring and outdated, hence has no chance in today's standards.

comments.author: bleakj
comments.body:
Back in 2014, there were "several" apps released every month.

Now in 2026 there are thousands daily - unless you've got a fantastic, hand-made application, and marketing to go along with it - you're going to need an immense amount of luck.
